items.claim: Declining to cluster 26:5-26:6 on the shared kesil token is correct: the word is genuinely pervasive across the whole fool-sequence rather than a bounding catchword.
items.evidence: collate.py confirms כְּסִֽיל at oshb:Prov.26.6 reaches BYTE tier. Independent resweep (sweep.py --skel kesil) of 26:1-26:11 finds the token in 10 of 11 verses (hits at 26:1,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10,11; only 26:2 lacks it) -- stronger than, though not identical to, the row's own 9-of-11 figure, whose list omits 26:8's dative-prefixed hit (the same construction the row already counts at 26:1). The object claimed (pervasive kesil, non-bounding) is verified; the digit variance does not change the correct conclusion. Cross-checked against the book's own genuine paired-contradiction case at 26:4-5 (אַל תַּ֣עַן כְּ֭סִיל כְּאִוַּלְתּ֑וֹ פֶּֽן תִּשְׁוֶה לּ֥וֹ גַם אָֽתָּה / עֲנֵ֣ה כְ֭סִיל כְּאִוַּלְתּ֑וֹ פֶּן יִהְיֶ֖ה חָכָ֣ם בְּעֵינָֽיו, an opposite-imperative construction, not a shared-token construction) -- confirms the row correctly withholds kesil from doing cohesion work it cannot bear.

items.claim: The proverb_cluster over 26:7-9 is well-grounded: 26:7 and 26:9 share a byte-identical closing colon that frames 26:8 as a deliberate inclusio, not ordinary catchword adjacency.
items.evidence: collate.py --json confirms the closing colon "וּ֝מָשָׁ֗ל בְּפִ֣י כְסִילִֽים" collates to BYTE tier against both the oshb:Prov.26.7 and oshb:Prov.26.9 windows independently -- the two verses' closing cola match down to every point and accent. Confirmed 26:8 does not itself carry this colon, so the frame genuinely brackets a single verse rather than repeating across three.

items.claim: Keeping 26:10 as a single_proverb and declining to cluster with 26:11 on the shared kesil token is sound, for the same pervasiveness grounds independently confirmed at 26:6.
items.evidence: collate.py confirms כְּ֝סִ֗יל at oshb:Prov.26.10 reaches BYTE tier. No construction-level link (shared colon, root pair, or disclosure object) ties 26:10 to 26:11 beyond the pervasive fool-word; each verse states its own complete image (indiscriminate wounding vs. dog-to-vomit).

items.claim: 26:11 is grammatically self-contained (an explicit prefixed comparison marker within the verse itself) and needs no adjacent verse; no cluster with 26:10 or 26:12 is warranted.
items.evidence: Verse text כְּ֭כֶלֶב שָׁ֣ב עַל קֵא֑וֹ כְּ֝סִ֗יל שׁוֹנֶ֥ה בְאִוַּלְתּֽוֹ carries its own comparison marker and completes the image within the verse, unlike the genuine split-simile case at 26:18-19 (see that row) where the apodosis marker ken is absent from the protasis verse. The 2 Peter 2:22 citation is correctly disclosed as background only, not boundary evidence.

items.claim: The bounded atsel catchword chain across 26:13-16 is byte-verified and genuinely bounded on both sides, distinct from the pervasive-theme trap the surrounding kesil verses illustrate.
items.evidence: sweep.py --skel atsel returns exactly Prov.26.13/14/15/16 in chapter 26 (4 verses; 16 book-wide) -- independently confirming both the back boundary the row discloses (absent at 26:17) and the front boundary the row does not explicitly state but which also holds (absent at 26:12). collate.py confirms BYTE tier for the full-verse quote at 26:14 (הַ֭דֶּלֶת תִּסּ֣וֹב עַל צִירָ֑הּ וְ֝עָצֵ֗ל עַל מִטָּתֽוֹ) and for the single-word forms at 26:13, 26:15, 26:16.

items.claim: The core claim is correct -- 26:18-19 is the sole comparative-simile pair in this part whose ken-apodosis sits in a different verse from its protasis -- but the row's own Hebrew quotation mixes tiers without disclosure.
items.evidence: Checked all six protasis/ken-apodosis comparisons in 25:1-27:27 directly against verse_map_oshb.json (26:1, 26:2, 26:8, 26:18-19, 27:8, 27:19): 26:1, 26:2, 26:8, 27:8, and 27:19 each carry both the protasis and the ken apodosis inside one verse; only 26:18/26:19 splits the pair across the seam -- the row's sole-instance claim and its five-verse comparison set are both accurate. However, the row quotes כֵּֽן (oshb:Prov.26.19) then continues with an unpointed 'ish' immediately after, presented as one continuous Hebrew phrase glossed together (so is the man). collate.py returns BYTE tier for כֵּֽן alone but only SKELETON tier for the unpointed fragment; the source is fully pointed (אִ֭ישׁ), and the skeleton-grade half of the quote is not labeled as such.
tier_citations: skeleton:oshb:Prov.26.19: quoted unpointed vs. source אִ֭ישׁ (undisclosed tier)

items.claim: The 26:20-21 pairing is genuine construction-level cohesion, not shared-theme over-clustering: the root pair etsim/esh recurs plain in v20 and prefixed in v21 in a deliberately inverted absence/presence image, and the K/Q and petuchah disclosures are both accurate.
items.evidence: collate.py confirms BYTE tier for עֵ֭צִים and אֵ֑שׁ (26:20) and for וְעֵצִ֣ים and לְאֵ֑שׁ (26:21). The ketiv/qere pair is verified inline in the source at 26:21 itself (מדונים unpointed immediately preceding the pointed qere מִ֝דְיָנִ֗ים), matching pmarks_Prov.json (kq=1 at Prov.26.21), and the identical pair recurs at 25:24 and 27:15 exactly as the row states. pmarks_Prov.json also confirms a PE (petuchah) mark at Prov.26.21, correctly disclosed as single-witness corroboration and not a driver.

items.claim: 26:22 is correctly classified as a non-header, single_proverb verse: verse-initial divrei is one of 5 such sites book-wide (only 30:1/31:1 are headers among 19 total divrei-bearing verses), and the claimed byte-identity with 18:8 is exact.
items.evidence: prov_device_inventory.json divrei_verse_initial lists exactly {12:6, 18:8, 26:22, 30:1, 31:1} (count 5); independent resweep (sweep.py --skel divrei) returns 19 book-wide, matching the row's cited figure exactly. A direct Python string-equality check of the raw OSHB verse text (stronger than collate tier alone) confirms Prov.18.8 and Prov.26.22 are character-for-character identical across every point and accent: דִּבְרֵ֣י נִ֭רְגָּן כְּמִֽתְלַהֲמִ֑ים וְ֝הֵ֗ם יָרְד֥וּ חַדְרֵי בָֽטֶן. The front-seam petuchah at 26:21 is correctly disclosed as corroborative-only (pmarks_Prov.json: Prov.26.21 = PE).
